cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: One Thing Leads to Another
cards.instruction: Use each small problem to justify solving a broader, more disruptive problem.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You put a folded napkin under that cafe chair, so I've put napkins under every leg. Shall we do the whole room?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only that one leg was short. Now you've raised the chair and it still wobbles.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally, we need the whole room level. We'll lift the floorboards and start underneath.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We open in twenty minutes. Take your napkins out and I'll deal with the short leg.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep yours in as the height marker. I'll tell the customers we're closed; we can level the counter while the floor's up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies a local shim everywhere; A3 interprets failed imitation as floor trouble; A5 preserves B shim as a model for wider leveling.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 remaining wobble makes A3 broaden cause; B4 opening pressure makes A5 choose closure.

relationship.evidence: B2 knows the local fix and B4 offers to do it while protecting opening.

heightening.evidence: A5 converts B4 simple fix into a height reference for counter work.

specificity.evidence: A1 chair/napkins and B2 short leg make the mistaken imitation visible through speech.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 closure and counter work are needed consequences, although height marker is deliberately misguided.
